newsitem.title: USA: Abundance of new growth in citrus belt - FASS.
newsitem.headline: Abundance of new growth in citrus belt - FASS.

text.p: Most groves in the Florida citrus belt are in good condition in spite of dry weather, the Florida Agricultural Statistics Service (FASS), said.
There were only a few light showers on the lower east coast providing an abundance of new growth in most well-cared for groves.
According to FASS, growers are irrigating to maintain good tree condition during the bloom period.
Caretakers are mowing, discing, and chopping following fertilizations and prior harvest operations. Hedging and topping are active in all areas.
FASS reported an estimated 18,000 boxes of navel oranges were harvested in the week ended March 2, down from 55,000 boxes the previous week and 110,000 boxes in the week ended February 16.
An estimated 3,818,000 boxes of early and mid oranges were harvested in the week ended March 2, down from 5,669,000 boxes the prior week and 7,239,000 boxes the week ended February 16, FASS said.
